extracted.intended_audience: scientists and researchers in oceanography, hydrography, and related natural sciences (also readers of general scientific journal reviews)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for collecting, processing, modelling, and diagrammatically representing sea-temperature (and related hydrographical) observations for routes and fixed points; includes methodological standards (interpolation, diagram choice, harmonic analysis) and recommended reporting practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpolation to obtain approximate data for given dates/localities
rubrics_metrics.description: From a large number of observations made at varying dates and, in the case of voluntary observations, at shifting points along particular lines — it is necessary in the first place to obtain, by interpolation, approximate data for given dates and localities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before diagrammatic representation, interpolate raw observations (which may be uneven in time and space) to produce comparable data for chosen dates and positions. This step is described as prerequisite to all subsequent plotting; no specific interpolation method mandated, but the need to standardize to given dates/localities is emphasised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose diagram type appropriate to question (Lalanne/time-distance isopleths for routes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Lalanne's method (coordinates: time and distance along a given line) with superposed contour lines or 'isopleths' representing temperature to portray surface temperatures along a route (e.g. Leith to Hamburg, January–December).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lalanne diagrams allow reading seasonal and spatial variations at a glance (e.g. extent of seasonal range, retardation of maxima/minima). Use when the interest is along a line of stations over successive months at a given depth (typically surface).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use time–depth isopleth diagrams for variations at a fixed point
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot temperature by means of isopleths over coordinates representing time and depth to show temperature changes at all depths during successive months at one fixed spatial point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These diagrams complement route-diagrams: Lalanne-type charts for along-route at one depth, time–depth charts for one point across depths. Choose the one matching whether the question is spatial variation along a line or vertical/temporal structure at a point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect observations at multiple depths, stations, and appropriate frequency (include salinity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain observations at all depths both as to temperature and to salinity from numerous stations (quarterly observations at many stations; monthly or six-weekly at others), and supplement with voluntary observations from passenger captains (surface temperature and occasional salinity samples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure wide spatial coverage (many stations along routes and off coasts), depth coverage (profiles), and temporal sampling (quarterly/monthly/six-weekly) to support interpolation and representation. Include salinity samples alongside temperature where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use harmonic (sine-curve) representation of annual temperature wave
rubrics_metrics.description: The rise and fall of surface temperature at a given point is a simple wave that can be suitably expressed as a sine-curve; the periodic temperature-function f(θ)=A0 + A1 sin(θ+e1) + A2 sin(2θ+e2)+… — in practice the first sine-factor differs but little from the actual curve and higher factors are negligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit a simple sine-formula to annual series (monthly means), reporting the three essential factors: mean temperature (A0), range or half-range (A1), and phase (e1, mean retardation of maximum/minimum). For multi-year means the sine-formula is even more closely applicable. Report numerical fit (e.g., maximal and mean discrepancies vs observations) to justify adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute and report harmonic constants for stations and transfer to diagrams/charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Work out harmonic constants (mean A0, amplitude A1, phase e1, etc.) for points (e.g., at one-degree longitude intervals along a route) and tabulate these constants; these can then be transferred to diagrams or charts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce tables of harmonic constants for adjoining stations or successive years to allow easy comparison and to serve as inputs for diagrammatic or chart representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify fit accuracy when using empirical/harmonic formulae
rubrics_metrics.description: When using the sine-formula or other empirical expressions, report numerical discrepancies between calculated results and observed means (e.g., 'results calculated from this formula for the middle points of the successive months differ in no case by so much as half a degree centigrade, and by a mean difference of only one-fifth of a degree').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State maximum and mean errors arising from the model and, if additional harmonic factors are included, show how much they reduce discrepancies (e.g., next factor reducing max discrepancy to ~0.25°). This quantification justifies use of the simpler model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use circular (phase) diagrams to visualise annual temperature wave
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sine-curve adequately represents the annual succession of temperatures, the diagram may be modified by substituting a circle on which time and temperature may be read together: centre height = mean temperature, radius = half-range, and a date-mark for phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Superpose such circles or combine them in a solid model to represent spatial changes in phase, mean and amplitude across points; this provides an alternate visual summary of mean, amplitude and phase together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report methods and apparatus clearly in experimental studies (artificial double refraction example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the operational relation R = C(T1 − T2)t (relative retardation) and the experimental arrangement (polarised light passed through a combination of glasses under flexure optically equivalent to a slab under uniform stress, analysis by Nicol and spectroscope; spectrum crossed by a dark band when R = integer × λ; measurement of λ gives R and C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the defining equations, the precise optical/measurement setup, how spectral features map to measured quantities (dark bands ↔ integer retardation), and how to compute the stress-optical coefficient C from measured R and known t and stress difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report wavelength and composition dependence and note systematic deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: When characterising properties (e.g., stress-optical coefficient C) report their dependence on the colour (wavelength) of light and on chemical composition (e.g., 'increase in percentage of B2O3 increases C; increased percentage of K2O probably decreases C'), and fit empirical formulae (hyperbolic law) while flagging local systematic deviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit an empirical law for wavelength dependence, present fitted constants, and explicitly note and investigate any systematic, local deviations (which may indicate effects analogous to absorption bands). Discuss dispersion of C and its relationship to composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supporting illustrative and documentary material in published works/editions
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations and facsimiles enhance the value and intelligibility of published works (e.g., an address on rolling stock is enhanced by seventy-six illustrations; descriptions of Maya manuscripts are of little value without consulting plates/facsimiles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include ample high-quality illustrations, plates or facsimiles where the subject is visual; ensure the reader can consult reproductions of original figures when describing or translating ancient manuscripts or detailing apparatus/observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain decipherment/conjectural method and indicate trustworthiness in editions of ancient documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Translations/commentaries of ancient manuscripts (e.g., the Dresden Codex) should indicate the process by which figures have been conjecturally deciphered and enable readers to assign the degree of trustworthiness to suggested readings; omission leaves the commentary of little value and renders suggested readings hard to assess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an explicit account of decipherment methodology, the evidential basis for readings, degrees of certainty or conjecture, and references to facsimiles; this is especially necessary in fields confined to a few experts where accepted explanations are not final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include comprehensive supporting data in expedition/station reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Expedition and station reports should include meteorological and botanical observations, tables of observations, records of temperature, plans and sketches, library catalogue, lists of species and descriptions of facilities (laboratories, aquarium, engine-house, docks), and any other material that adds to reproducibility or usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tabulated observational data, maps/plots, plans and sketches of stations or routes, and catalogues; these supporting materials increase the scientific and practical value of published reports and provide guidance for future observers.
